entries.title: Young British men lose £11bn in the ‘Moneysphere’
entries.summary: Survey of 2,000 UK Gen Z males found 44% fell victim to investment scams via social media, losing combined £11bn (average £5,000 each). The 'Moneysphere' comprises anonymous accounts, influencers and AI creators promoting get-rich-quick schemes. Young men targeted multiple times daily; 18-24-year-olds 1.64 times more likely victims than average.

entries.title: Investigation underway into DWP cyber incident as services taken offline
entries.summary: UK Department for Work and Pensions took services offline following cyber incident detected yesterday. Investigation underway with National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre. Currently no evidence of data loss or malicious actor involvement. Regular benefit and pension payments unaffected. Websites for pensions, universal credit and PIP impacted.

entries.title: Understanding Violent and Non-Violent Right-Wing Extremist Activity Online: Part III – Implications and Future Directions
entries.summary: Three-part research series on online posting behaviours of violent and non-violent right-wing extremists. This final part explores implications and future directions. Project aimed to develop risk-factor frameworks for law enforcement, intelligence agencies and tech companies to identify credible online threats beyond existing studies lacking comparison groups.

entries.title: America Needs Homegrown Open-Weight Models
entries.summary: No text supplied. Article title suggests discussion of open-weight artificial intelligence models and their development or deployment in the United States.

entries.title: Leaked EU Draft Would Allow Mass Scanning of Private Messages
entries.summary: Leaked EU draft deal on Child Sexual Abuse Regulation ('Chat Control 2.0') reveals provision allowing 'independent administrative authority' to order mass scanning of private messages for up to 24 months without court order. Irish Presidency reportedly attempting to bypass Parliament negotiators. Final trilogue meeting scheduled December 8.

entries.title: USAID Files: Staff Said Taxpayers Were Footing Big Tech’s Disinformation Bill
entries.summary: USAID Files show January 2021 conversation where officials noted agency's anti-disinformation work effectively subsidised Big Tech by using taxpayer money to fund organisations flagging content to platforms. Officials suggested platforms should share costs rather than government ceasing funding. USAID monitors and flags content in Ethiopia, Ukraine, Moldova and Kenya.

entries.title: USAID Files: The Agency Wanted a Direct Line to Facebook for Takedowns
entries.summary: USAID Files reveal US government agency had direct access to Meta's policy team for content removal requests. November 2022 instance shows USAID official flagged Guatemalan page; Meta removed one violating post despite page overall complying with standards. USAID sought to establish 'streamlined' direct channels between Missions and Meta for future takedowns.

entries.title: USAID Files: Google Told US Officials It Might Rethink Twitter’s Place in Search
entries.summary: USAID Files show December 2022 State Department meeting where Google told US counter-disinformation officials it might reconsider Twitter's inclusion in Google Search carousel if Twitter handled moderation differently during elections. Meeting attended by Google Trust & Safety VP and State Department representatives from twelve bureaux.

entries.title: Russia’s Unconventional War on Europe: Sabotage, Deterrence and Future Scenarios
entries.summary: IISS report examines Russia's unconventional war on Europe through sabotage targeting critical infrastructure. Despite Russian intelligence services' campaign, European military support for Ukraine continues, defence spending rose 12.6% in 2025, and NATO expanded surveillance. Report presents four scenarios to 2029.

entries.title: ICO reprimands Home Office over data inaccuracy in border system
entries.summary: ICO reprimanded Home Office for inaccurate data in Helios border system, developed with BAE Systems. Investigation found no measures to correct inaccuracies before launch, staff instructed not to include personal information in rectification requests, and uncertainty whether staff knew how to report errors.

entries.title: How Long Is Long Enough? Crime Reporting Delays, Investigative Timing, and a Benchmark for Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) Data Retention
entries.summary: Examines Automated Licence Plate Reader data retention periods and their relationship to crime reporting delays and investigative timing. Analyses 3.32 million records to establish benchmark for appropriate retention periods.

entries.summary: Covers briefing on state attorneys general suing SpaceX regarding Grok deepfakes.

entries.title: The Price of Cost-Cutting: What Next for UK Aid and Development Assistance?
entries.summary: Deep UK and Western aid cuts are fuelling insecurity across sub-Saharan Africa. Protecting British interests requires money paired with genuine strategic reform.

entries.summary: Japan's education ministry disclosed a hacker breach of its government procurement system, potentially exposing business information and email addresses.

entries.summary: SAP confirmed a cybersecurity incident after reports that hackers infiltrated its software development infrastructure, potentially accessing the company's source code.
